summary: 51 units reviewed, 25 marked fix (all with machine patches) plus one human-only remark on u43. Severity: 10 error issues (u8 English/Hindi disagree on what yantra-baddha-talam qualifies; u12 daṇḍa-upanata = submitting with his army, not 'to force'; u28/u29 kṣāra = sugar in supply lists, not alkali; u32 subject and mood: the weak king gets the enemy's guard relaxed, not 'the enemy would'), 36 minor (bracketed glosses inside the Hindi in 12 units against the glossary rule; small additions 'one', 'की मूर्ति', 'बनाकर', 'उसके विरुद्ध', supplied 'to the enemy'; missing prefixes in gram labels; prarūpayet not causative; alternative construals noted for u16, u42). Both text_flags (u1 daivata.ijyāyāṃ, u51 dvāḥsthān) are right. u1 corrupt compound is handled well (medium confidence, editors' doubt mark kept as a separate token). u43 prāśya-prāśa stays obscure and needs a person; u21 ākṣikavad apakṣepeṇa is honestly marked uncertain. u23 pravāsita 'put to death' agrees with the text's usage. No regrouping suggested (41-42 are one sentence but keep the edition's numbering). Glossary extended with the chapter's recurring terms.
